part.text:
Both use `Arrays.equals` on float arrays (bit-level comparison, consistent with their `Arrays.hashCode`-based hashCodes), so no further changes needed.

Summary of the fix:

- **`lucene/core/src/java/org/apache/lucene/geo/XYPoint.java:72-73`** — `equals` now uses `Float.compare(point.x, x) == 0 && Float.compare(point.y, y) == 0` instead of `==`, so `-0.0` and `0.0` are no longer considered equal while their `Float.hashCode`-based hashCodes differ (the assertEquals contract violation).
- **`lucene/core/src/java/org/apache/lucene/geo/XYCircle.java:81-83`** — same fix for `x`, `y`, and `radius`, matching its `Float.hashCode`-based hashCode.
- `XYRectangle` already used `Float.compare` (consistent with its `floatToIntBits` hashCode), and `XYLine`/`XYPolygon` use bit-level `Arrays.equals`, so they were left unchanged.

Verification: Gradle hangs in this container (no network for dependency resolution), so I compiled `lucene/core` with javac and ran a harness replicating the failing scenarios: targeted `-0.0`/`0.0` cases for XYPoint/XYCircle/XYRectangle plus 4M randomized pairs checking the `equals` ↔ `Float.compare` correspondence and the `equals` ⇒ equal-`hashCode` contract — all passed.
